checks.claim: LUT/FF and routing are separate FPGA resource classes; architecture is series-specific.
Generic HDL recommended; RTL syntax alone does not guarantee one specific CLB resource mapping.
Incomplete combinational assignment can infer an unintended latch.
Icarus uses iverilog compilation and vvp execution for Verilog simulation.
Nonblocking assignments schedule later LHS updates after RHS evaluation; clocked coding style avoids races.
7 Series devices include wide multiplexer resources; LUT mapping depends on design and tools.
Local generated clocks need suitable routing/constraints; clock enables are preferable when staying in a single domain.
Reset startup synchronization and controlled release require design-specific care.
Functional HDL simulation and testbench use iverilog plus vvp; verification must establish actual assertions.
SPI CPOL/CPHA define idle level and leading/trailing capture edges.
NXP UM10204 Rev 7 defines START/STOP, ninth ACK, clock stretching and bus clear.
24LC256 does not ACK while internal write cycle is in progress; ACK polling determines readiness rather than assuming clock stretch.
Vivado UG901 differentiates synchronous RAM inference and port read/write modes; physical collision depends on the RAM primitive.
UltraScale block memory address collisions require matching documented clock/port/mode conditions; cannot infer safe dual-clock read-first behavior.
Routing-based data path max and min delays drive setup and hold analysis.
Use recognizable CDC synchronizer circuits and ASYNC_REG attributes; report_cdc and report_synchronizer_mtbf help review.
Gray bus transfers may need max_delay -datapath_only or bus skew; check precedence of clock group exceptions.
set_input_delay and set_output_delay min/max describe external interface timing, not a local FPGA FF setup number.
Vivado 2026.1 moved to tiered licensing; BASIC remains free and supports both Windows and Linux within its tier scope.
Non-project Tcl supports read_verilog/read_xdc, synthesis, place, route, reporting and bitstream commands.
An MMCM/PLL output frequency is synthesized from device-dependent multiply/divide factors as Fout = Fin x M / (D x O); legal factor ranges and VCO limits are device specific.
FIFO Generator offers both a Native interface and an AXI4-Stream interface, and its First-Word Fall-Through option changes when the first word appears on dout.
Block Memory Generator selects Read-First, Write-First or No-Change behavior for a same-clock simultaneous read and write on one port.
MicroBlaze is a configurable soft processor with optional FPU, MMU and caches, and exposes AXI interfaces.
Vivado IP Integrator Block Design with Block/Connection Automation instantiates the processor, interconnect, clock/reset and debug blocks, and Create HDL Wrapper emits a synthesizable top level.
Vitis builds a platform and BSP from the exported hardware description, providing base-address macros and peripheral drivers to the application.
RV32I base integer instructions are fixed 32-bit encodings using six formats (R/I/S/B/U/J) with the opcode in bits [6:0] and x0 hardwired to zero.
The riscv-gnu-toolchain project provides RISC-V gcc/binutils tooling, including objcopy, for producing memory images.
PCI Express link rates are specified per generation as 2.5, 5.0, 8.0, 16.0 and 32.0 GT/s, with 8b/10b coding for Gen1/Gen2 and 128b/130b for Gen3 and later.
Integrated FPGA transceivers provide the coding, serialization, transmit/receive equalization and clock-data recovery, and their supported line rates are documented per device family.

High-level synthesis separates scheduling (which clock cycle each operation runs in) from binding (which hardware resource it uses), with pragmas such as PIPELINE, UNROLL and ARRAY_PARTITION guiding the microarchitecture.
The Vitis HLS flow includes C simulation, C synthesis producing an RTL estimate, and C/RTL co-simulation that compares the C model against the generated RTL.
Vivado functionality is driven by Tcl commands, documented in the Vivado Tcl Command Reference (UG835), so scripts generated by an LLM can be validated by running them.
The Model Context Protocol is an open protocol for exposing external tools and data sources to LLM applications.
AMD UG949 treats clock-domain-crossing and design constraints as explicit methodology items rather than something synthesis auto-corrects.
The conventional 640x480@60 display timing uses a 25.175 MHz pixel clock with 800 total pixels per line and 525 total lines per frame, as tabulated by VESA display timing standards.
Luma coefficients for RGB to grayscale conversion are defined in ITU-R BT.601 as approximately 0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B, which the fixed-point weights 77/150/29 scaled by 256 approximate.
External DDR memory interfaces on 7 series FPGAs are implemented with the Memory Interface Generator as documented in UG586.

limitations: Code simulation does not establish board-level timing.
Proposed FPGA logic and timing figures are conceptual; no hardware measurements are claimed.
No synthesis resource usage, power or Fmax benchmark is asserted.
UART, SPI and I2C examples are intentionally scoped teaching units, not production protocol IP.
Chapter 14 STA numbers are arithmetic examples, not measured or Vivado-reported slack.
Chapter 15 Tcl is a guarded demonstration; no vendor build or board programming is claimed.
